title: `RecordContextValue.dataSource` is declared `string` while every producer passes a DataSource ADAPTER — a published type that every consumer has to cast away
body:
Found while fixing objectui#8883 (dev seat). Filed rather than folded in: the repair touches `@object-ui/react`'s published context type and every consumer that casts around it, which is a different package and a wider blast radius than that card's fence.

## The contract, quoted

`packages/react/src/context/RecordContext.tsx:112-118`:

```ts
export interface RecordContextValue {
  objectName: string;
  recordId: string | number | null | undefined;
  /** Optional datasource id; mirrors the page-level datasource override. */
  dataSource?: string;
```

`RecordContextValue` is exported from `@object-ui/react` — it is a published type, and that comment is a published statement about what the member holds.

## What every producer actually puts there

`RecordDetailView` — the production host — forwards its `dataSource: any` ADAPTER prop straight through (`packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx:69` declares the prop, `:2374` passes it into `RecordContextProvider`). Nothing anywhere in the repo assigns a datasource ID string to this member.

## What every consumer therefore has to do

Read it off the instrument rather than off a number written here:

```
git grep -n "ctx as any)?\.dataSource\|ctx?\.dataSource as any\|ctx!\.dataSource as any" -- packages | grep -v '\.test\.'
```

Every hit is a cast that exists only because the declared type is wrong, spanning `@object-ui/fields`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail` and `@object-ui/app-shell`. The sibling spelling (`ctx?.dataSource` handed to a prop typed as `DataSource`) type-checks today only because those props are `any` at the receiving end.

`DataSource` itself is fully declared in `packages/types/src/data.ts:350`, with `getObjectSchema` a REQUIRED member at `:539` — so the honest type is available, imported by these very packages, and not used here.

## Why it costs something

The cast is not free: it deletes the compiler's answer to "does this adapter have the method I am about to call". objectui#8883 is a live instance — the rail reaches for `dataSource.getObjectSchema` through `(ctx as any)`, and the reason an author must go read `packages/types/src/data.ts` to learn whether that member is guaranteed is precisely that the context type says `string`. Two cards in one week (objectui#8882, objectui#8883) added a metadata read through this member; the next one will cast too.

## Deliberately NOT claimed here

- Whether the right repair is to type the member as `DataSource`, or to keep a separate `dataSourceId?: string` for the override the comment describes and add the adapter beside it. The comment says the member mirrors a page-level datasource OVERRIDE, which reads like a real requirement that simply never landed — whoever takes this should find out whether any producer ever set an ID here, and say so, before choosing.
- Whether the `as any` casts should all go in the same change or follow the type. The type is the defect; the casts are its symptom count.
